site_or_subject: Virginia datacenter industry: residential bill impact (JLARC Report 598)
record: JLARC (9 Dec 2024) estimated a typical Dominion residential customer could see generation and transmission costs rise $14-$37 per month by 2040 (constant dollars) under unconstrained datacenter demand; Virginia datacenters use ~5,050 MW (about 2 million households' electricity) and unconstrained demand could double within 10 years. One-third of sites are near residential areas; datacenters emit low-frequency noise that is 'not loud enough to damage nearby residents' hearing', and local noise ordinances carry a maximum civil penalty of $500.

site_or_subject: PJM capacity auctions: revenue attributable to datacenter load (Independent Market Monitor)
record: The IMM (1 Oct 2025) estimated that including 11,993 MW of existing and forecast datacenter load raised 2026/2027 Base Residual Auction revenues by $7,271,197,971, an 82.1% increase over the revenues without that load; total 2026/2027 BRA revenues were $16,124,370,889. Datacenter load raised 2025/2026 BRA revenues by $9,332,103,858, a combined $16,603,301,829 across the two auctions. In the market monitor's 2025 State of the Market report, the capacity component of the total cost of wholesale power rose from $2,834 million (2024) to $10,616 million (2025), +274.6% (ledger arithmetic: 10,616 / 2,834 - 1); per MWh of load it rose from $3.61 to $13.09 (+262.3%, as stated by the IMM), from 6.5% to 15.8% of the total.

site_or_subject: CRU Large Energy Users connection policy for datacenters
operator: Commission for Regulation of Utilities (CRU); EirGrid/ESB Networks
record: CRU's proposed decision CRU/202504 (18 Feb 2025) recorded datacenters at ~21% of national electricity demand in 2023, and data centre and new technology load at 7.1 TWh of 30.5 TWh national demand; ~30% by 2030-32 (13.3 TWh in 2032), and ~50% of electricity produced in Dublin/Meath; it did not quantify network-cost impacts on consumers. The final decision CRU/2025236 (12 Dec 2025) [as summarised by Matheson LLP; the CRU's decision paper itself was not found] requires datacenters with MIC >=10 MVA to provide dispatchable onsite or proximate generation/storage at least equal to MIC (subject to de-rating), requires datacenters at or above the 1 MVA de-minimis level to meet >=80% of annual demand with additional Irish renewables on a 6-year glide path from energisation, and limits new datacenters to one-year capacity contracts.

site_or_subject: Meta hyperscale datacenter, Zeewolde: state land sale
record: The Meta site included land of which the State owned 'a large part' (Council of State, 2023); NOS put the State share at about 80 ha [press, source not named: NOS]. The Eerste Kamer adopted a motion on 21 Dec 2021 (35925 XIV, H) asking the government to have the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf suspend sales of agricultural land for hyperscale datacenters. In the 22 Feb 2022 Senate interpellation the minister said the State still held the land as a private-law party but would not undo the municipal permit. Minister De Jonge's letter of 10 June 2022 (Kamerstuk 26 643 nr. 862) transmitted TNO's assessment of the municipality's plan against the Aug 2021 sale conditions. The same day the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf wrote to Zeewolde that it could not sell the land on the current assessment. TNO found the design energy-efficient for now, with intelligent cooling and no drinking water used for cooling, but roofs, facades and surrounding land not maximally used for solar, rainwater use unclear and the residual-heat plan too undeveloped to assess. On 20 Sep 2023 the Council of State annulled the Trekkersveld IV zoning plan (ECLI:NL:RVS:2023:3550), noting that neither the municipality nor the initiator owned the land and that there was no certainty the State would sell.

site_or_subject: Redata special tax regime for datacenters: official fiscal cost estimate
record: Senate budget note NT 33/2025 (23 Sept 2025) on MP 1.318/2025 describes counterparts of >=10% capacity to the domestic market and 2% of acquisitions to R&D, and mentions no job figures. The Câmara approved a substitute text of PL 278/2026 on 24 Feb 2026 and sent it to the Senate; it became Lei 15.504 of 15 Sept 2026, which requires beneficiaries to meet all their electricity demand from renewable or low-emission sources (art. 11-B §1º III), to invest 2% of the value of products acquired under the regime in research, development and innovation, with at least 40% going to programmes in the North, Northeast and Centre-West (art. 11-I), and to make at least 10% of effective processing supply available to the domestic market (art. 11-B §1º I); both commitments are reduced by 20% for establishments in those regions (§7º). It also requires a water usage effectiveness 'igual ou inferior a 0,05 L/kWh', measured annually (§1º IV).
